V3 builds a full explanatory structure with related work, dataset and task definitions, method, results, and an organized supplement with contents. Although the abstract and concluding narrative remain largely unchanged, the document's organization and explanatory development change substantially.

P2.justification: The opening schematic is retained, while v3 adds graph diagrams, a detailed pipeline illustration, structured performance tables, ablation charts, illustrated success/failure cases, and prompt tables. These provide substantial new visual explanations and comparison displays beyond v1's single figure.

R1.justification: V3 adds a dedicated related-work section covering multimodal RAG, MMKGs, and graph retrieval. New references such as Wiki-LLaVA, Plan-on-Graph, and G-Retriever support a substantially fuller account of how the approach extends autonomous graph-search ideas to multimodal knowledge. Earlier introductory positioning is retained.

T1.justification: V1 contains no mathematical formulation. V3 introduces formal graph, attribute, query and ground-truth definitions, information assumptions for three task variants, and recursive subgraph-expansion and loop-handling rules in Sections 3-4. This substantially adds formal specification, although neither version provides theorems or proofs.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves v1's central weakness: empirical claims and a proposed retriever presented without inspectable experimental or implementation support. The benchmark comparisons, diagnostic analyses, judging checks, and detailed prompts substantially improve assessability and reproducibility. Reporting problems remain, including Section 5.2's vanilla ranking contradicting Table 3 and missing repeated-run accuracy uncertainty, but they do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MH-MMKG, the 238-question Monster Hunter benchmark, and a training-free multi-agent retriever. All pages are readable, including v3's supplementary material. V1 is a complete three-page overview without appendices; its limited procedural detail constrains judgments about underlying method changes.

after.justification: V3 reports original model and human benchmark results, ablations, human validation of automated judging, and computational-cost measurements in Section 5 and the supplement.

before.justification: V1's abstract and introduction report improved performance from the authors' experiments on open- and closed-source MLLMs, and its conclusion reports findings about perception and retrieval. These are qualitative empirical outcomes only; no scores or detailed experimental evidence are presented.

results.title: Taming the Untamed: Graph-Based Knowledge Retrieval and Reasoning for MLLMs to Conquer the Unknown

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same structural-modeling and sequence-length-adaptation contributions, novelty claim, and headline accuracies. The appendix adds supporting evidence without redefining the main claims.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses potential benefits of multi-scale designs. Section 11 adds a specific failure condition—unclear segmentation boundaries—attributes it to single-scale features, and proposes hierarchical Mamba as future work. The appendix also adds interpretations of state specialization and hyperparameter sensitivity.

D1.justification: v1 provides basic architectural and sampling settings but defers further details. Section 8 and Algorithm 1 add tensor dimensions, block operations, downstream heads, optimizer and scheduler settings, training budgets, warm-up, voting details, and pretraining hardware and runtime: one RTX A6000 and approximately 18 hours. These substantially improve documentation of retained experiments.

E1.justification: Section 9.2 adds training and evaluation on ScanNetV2 for large-scale scene-level 3D object detection. This substantially extends the earlier object-level classification, few-shot classification, and part-segmentation coverage, which is retained.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds 3DETR and 3DETR-m as detection comparators alongside Point-M2AE. Comparator membership in the original classification, segmentation, and few-shot tables remains unchanged, making this a focused extension of the baseline set.

E3.justification: The added detection evaluation introduces 2048 input tokens, 128 spatial states, 1080 pretraining epochs, batch size 16, and mAP25/mAP50 metrics. Figures 4–5 also introduce token-length sweeps for computational cost and inference speed. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish changes to their protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v3 adds serialization comparisons, spatial-state-count and convolution-neighborhood sensitivity studies, and training without pretraining. It also adds efficiency scaling analyses and visual studies of state correlations, reconstruction, and segmentation, substantially broadening validation.

E5.justification: Both versions report few-shot means and standard deviations over 10 independent experiments. The appendix repeats that practice; it introduces no additional seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New results include 67.8 mAP25 and 50.6 mAP50 on ScanNetV2, per-category segmentation scores, sensitivity results, training-from-scratch scores, and efficiency curves. Table 8 separately reports official-code reproductions of PointGPT-S and PointMamba; their original Table 2 scores remain, so these are additional results rather than established same-setting performance changes.

M1.justification: The spatial states, position-dependent state updates, lightweight convolutions, bidirectional processing, adaptive sampling interval, and consistency loss remain unchanged. Appendix Algorithm 1 expands implementation documentation of the existing block; the new detection experiment does not establish a revised core method.

P1.justification: The original narrative and section order are largely unchanged. v3 updates author/contact information, adds an acknowledgment and an organized appendix, and makes small caption and cross-reference edits. Implementation explanations expand, but the main paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8–12, an unnumbered pretraining comparison table, Algorithm 1, and Figures 4–8. These include efficiency plots and extensive qualitative displays. The original figures and tables largely retain their presentation, but the added displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Adam, SGDR, and additional 3D detection and representation-learning works. The related-work discussion and positioning against point-based, Transformer-based, and Mamba-based approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the SSM reasoning remain unchanged. Appendix Equations 14–15 explicitly state standard classification and segmentation cross-entropy losses; no substantive new mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited implementation documentation and lack of large-scene evaluation and quantitative efficiency curves. The appendix supplies reproducibility details, targeted ablations, ScanNetV2 detection evidence, and explicit segmentation limitations while preserving the original results. These gains materially strengthen assessability and empirical support; minor appendix cross-reference errors do not outweigh them.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StruMamba3D and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables. v1 ends with references; v3 retains the main paper and adds an appendix. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ScanNetV2 detection results, further ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in the appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original classification, part-segmentation, few-shot classification, and ablation results for StruMamba3D.

results.title: StruMamba3D: Exploring Structural Mamba for Self-supervised Point Cloud Representation Learning

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same dataset, pipeline and generalization claims. The claim of outperforming GPT-3.5-Turbo on all five OOD benchmarks also remains, despite both versions' Table 5 reporting lower TEMPLAMA accuracy: 21.43 versus 33.67.

C2.justification: The supplement expands the rationale for general-purpose tools and LCS matching, explains the computational motivation for initial caption/OCR use, and states evaluation boundaries involving image answers and externally supplied OCR tokens. Main-text interpretations of model bottlenecks and errors remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies substantial previously absent reproduction information: tool backends and interfaces in Table 8, construction of 34 examples from 150 user scenarios, matching pseudocode, prompt templates, LoRA training settings and hardware, and detailed evaluation and answer-matching procedures. These are disclosures about the existing work; the code-access URL is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ToolVQA and the same five OOD benchmarks: TextVQA, TallyQA, InfoSeek, GTA and TEMPLAMA. Supplementary participant descriptions and example galleries document existing data collection and coverage rather than new populations or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark, OOD, few-shot and ablation tables. Newly cited software and tool implementations in the supplement are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The existing splits, evaluation modes, model settings and metrics are retained. Section 9 newly specifies the 1,622 text-answer end-to-end examples, OOD subsampling and TextVQA OCR-token exclusion, but presents these as details of existing experiments rather than revised protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds a descriptive analysis of real users' tool frequencies, supporting toolset selection and allowing comparison with the dataset frequencies in Figure 5. Existing ablations and error analysis are unchanged; Figures 9–10 provide illustrative trajectories rather than new robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Additional annotation and sampling details do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values and rankings. New descriptive results include Figure 8's user frequencies, such as Search at 30.8% and Caption at 23.6%, and Section 9.2's statement that tool-use VQA takes approximately 4–6 times as long as conventional VQA.

M1.justification: The DFS pipeline, LCS-based example selection and fine-tuning objective are unchanged. The supplement documents implementation choices, including initial ImageCaption/OCR use, LoRA and controller prompts; it does not establish a version-to-version change in the procedure.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain essentially unchanged apart from citation renumbering and text reflow. v2 adds an organized supplement with an overview, procedural explanations and prompt transcripts, extending the supporting structure without extensively rewriting the paper.

P2.justification: The supplement substantially expands visual documentation through Table 8, Algorithm 1, the user-frequency chart and two organized galleries showing trajectories and answer annotations. Figure 9 expands some examples already illustrated in Figure 3. Existing main-paper figures and tables retain their presentation.

R1.justification: All 50 original references are retained, with 11 additions supporting supplementary implementation and evaluation details, including LoRA, XTuner, OpenCompass, OCRBench and Tree of Thoughts. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, training loss and LCS-based retrieval expression are unchanged. Algorithm 1 supplies standard dynamic-programming pseudocode for the already specified LCS operation, without adding a theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision.

improvement.justification: The supplement addresses important reproducibility omissions in v1 by specifying tool implementations, prompts, data-construction procedures, training settings and evaluation subsets. This substantially improves readers' ability to inspect and reproduce the central contribution without changing benchmark performance. There are flaws: Figure 9 gives '26' for an apple-producing-area question whose tool output says 'Washington', and the existing OOD overclaim remains uncorrected. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in methodological transparency.

A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolVQA dataset and ToolEngine pipeline. Text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable. v1 ends after its references; v2 retains the main paper and adds supplementary Sections 6–11.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports the user tool-use frequency distribution in Figure 8.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, data-construction and training ablations, few-shot experiments, and error analysis in Tables 3–7 and Figure 7.
